drawer.confidenceHelp: Fist to five: instead of a metric you enter a level from 1 to 5 — “{low}” to “{high}”. Scale and target are fixed; below 3 the goal is replanned. For goals that no single number can measure.
drawer.freiesLabelDerMessgroesse: Free-text label for the measure, e.g. customers or units. With metric type Custom it is appended as a suffix to every displayed value.
drawer.gewichtImRollupDes: Weight in the parent goal's rollup (empty = 1)
drawer.wieStarkDiesesUnterziel: How much this sub-goal counts in the parent goal's average. Empty = 1 (all sub-goals weighted equally).
drawer.verantwortlichFuerDiesesZiel: Accountable for this goal. From the tenant's users.
drawer.worausSichDerFortschritt: How progress is calculated: Manual (you maintain the value yourself), From sub-goals (average of the children), KPI tree (leaf: actuals from linked epic KPIs; branch: sub-goal values cascade up, measured by value) or Confidence vote (fist to five instead of a metric).
drawer.zaehltNichtImAutomatischen: Excluded from this goal's automatic progress
drawer.kpiTreeBranch: KPI tree as a branch: the sub-goals' values cascade upward, and attainment is measured by value (value reached ÷ target) rather than as an average of the sub-goals. Each sub-goal needs its conversion factor into this unit — without it, it contributes nothing.
drawer.kpiTreeLeaf: KPI tree as a leaf: the actual comes from the linked epic KPIs (Δ × factor). Without a link the goal stays at 0%.
drawer.kpiTreeLeafNoPortfolio: KPI tree as a leaf draws its actual from linked epic KPIs — and the portfolio module is not enabled here. With sub-goals the mode works without it: their values cascade up and attainment is measured by value.
drawer.rollupHelp: Progress = weighted average of the sub-goals. A metric of its own is ignored.
drawer.kpiLinkHelp: The KPIs of linked epics form this goal's actual value via Δ × conversion factor (progress source “KPI tree”).

errors.kpiAlreadyDrives: This KPI already drives another goal — a KPI can drive only one.

myApprovals.alleFreigabenDieAktuell: All approvals currently waiting on your decision.

hypothesisDrafted.label: Benefit hypothesis is drafted
hypothesisDrafted.help: The benefit hypothesis describes the expected benefit and the assumption behind it. Write it on the Hypothesis tab. It is approved with the sign-off of this step — there is no separate approval run before that.

hypothesisApproved.label: Benefit hypothesis is approved
hypothesisApproved.help: The hypothesis was signed off with the step to L1. Without that stamp the epic never passed cleanly through L1.

ownerNominated.label: Epic owner is named
ownerNominated.help: The epic owner is accountable for progress, business case and approvals. Name them on the Overview via the owner field.

businessCaseDrafted.label: Business case is drafted
businessCaseDrafted.help: The business case records cost, benefit and options. Maintain it on the Business case tab. It is approved with the sign-off of this step by the five parties — there is no separate approval run before that.

deliverablesDrafted.label: Deliverables are cut
deliverablesDrafted.help: The epic is broken down into child features. Cut them on the Deliverables tab — they later carry the implementation and the effort estimate.

dependenciesMapped.label: Dependencies are recorded
dependenciesMapped.help: Dependencies on other initiatives are entered on the Dependencies tab. They determine what has to be finished before this epic.

kpisDefined.label: KPIs are defined
kpisDefined.help: At least one metric with a baseline and a target exists on the KPI & benefit tab. The realised benefit is measured against it later.

budgetAllocated.label: Budget is allocated (Σ > 0)
budgetAllocated.help: Budget has been allocated to the epic through participatory budgeting (sum > 0). The allocation happens in the budgeting periods.

featureStarted.label: At least one feature has started
featureStarted.help: At least one child feature is in progress. Features are created on the Deliverables tab; their status is set in the delivery cockpit.

featuresCompleted.label: All child features are completed
featuresCompleted.help: All child features are completed — the usual indication that the implementation is done. The confirmation is made by the sign-off, not by the counter. You maintain the feature status in the delivery cockpit.

implementationConfirmed.label: Implementation is confirmed as complete (L4.2)
implementationConfirmed.help: Completion of the implementation was requested and signed off (step L4.2). Only afterwards can the realised impact be confirmed (L5).

intendedClassSet.label: The epic is classified
intendedClassSet.help: Portfolio epic or ART epic — what do you expect? This is an expectation, not a decision: the class arises later from the costs in the approved business case. Set it in the overview under “Classification”.

goalLinked.label: Linked to a goal
goalLinked.help: Which goal does this endeavour pay into? Without that link the KPI chain starts nowhere, and in the end no benefit can be demonstrated. Set it in the overview under “Strategic contributions”.

detailing.label: Idea captured
detailing.description: Epic created in the funnel, waiting to be reviewed.
detailing.milestoneApprover: The VMO reviews the epic and names the epic owner

hypothesis.label: Work out the hypothesis
hypothesis.description: Problem, target group, expected benefit, leading indicators.
hypothesis.milestoneApprover: VMO — the sign-off is at the same time the release

analyzing.label: Schedule for analysis
analyzing.description: The value stream decides what gets effort.

businessCase.label: Work out the business case
businessCase.description: Create the lean business case and submit it for release.
businessCase.milestoneApprover: Architect lead · business owner · finance · IRT · VMO · product manager

implementationStarted.label: Start the implementation
implementationStarted.description: Get the first feature under way.
implementationStarted.milestoneApprover: VMO — plus product manager for ART epics

implementation.label: Implement
implementation.description: Deliver features until the initiative stands.

done.label: Measure the benefit
done.description: Is the initiative working as promised?

nextStep.waitingHint: The maturity change has been requested. The named people decide next; until then the related content is locked.
nextStep.hypothesisHint: On the hypothesis tab, describe the problem, target group, expected benefit and leading indicators — so the approvers have a basis for their decision.
nextStep.requestL1Hint: The content is there. Request the maturity change to L1 — its sign-off is at the same time the release of the benefit hypothesis.
nextStep.analysisHint: The hypothesis is released. Request selection for analysis — the value stream decides what gets effort. The maturity level stays at L1.
nextStep.requestL2Hint: The content is there. Request the change to L2 — the sign-off by the five parties is the release of the business case.
nextStep.businessCaseHint: Detail the business case (cost, benefit, assumptions, risks) before you submit it for release.
nextStep.investmentHintBudgeting: Budget is allocated. Request the change to L3 — that signs off the investment decision by name.
nextStep.investmentHintPlain: Request the change to L3 — that signs off the investment decision by name, by VMO and finance.
nextStep.allocateHint: The business case is released. Now plan budget for this epic in controlling so the investment can be signed off.
nextStep.firstFeatureHint: The investment is signed off. Create features on the deliverables tab and start the first one in a PI — that moves the epic to L4.
nextStep.impactHint: The implementation is confirmed as complete. Request the change to L5 — controlling signs off that the forecast benefit has arrived on the balance sheet or in the KPIs.
nextStep.confirmHint: All features are completed. Request the step to L4.2 — that signs off the finished implementation and sets the actual date.
nextStep.finishFeaturesHint: Implementation is running. Complete the remaining features — after that the finished implementation (L4.2) can be confirmed.
nextStep.createFeaturesHint: There are no child features on the epic yet. Create some on the deliverables tab and start them.

rtb.wasDieserWertstromLaufend: What this value stream needs on an ongoing basis appears here — once the first item exists.

rtb.mitArtZaehltDie: With an ART the item counts directly against it. Without an ART and without a solution it is spread evenly across all ARTs of the value stream.

platformAdmin.mission: You run Pulse across tenants: you provision workspaces, enable modules and keep operations healthy.
platformAdmin.neueKundenWorkspacesBereitstellen: Provision new customer workspaces and enable their modules.
platformAdmin.mitgliedschaftenUndPlattformAdminrechte: Manage memberships and platform admin rights across all tenants.
platformAdmin.betriebsstoerungenErkennenBevorDie: Spot operational trouble before customers report it.
platformAdmin.duUebergibstAnDen: You hand over to the tenant admin: once the workspace exists, they set up users, roles and the organisation.
platformAdmin.deineArbeitLiegtAusserhalb: Your work lies outside this workspace
platformAdmin.alsEinzigeRolleArbeitest: You are the only role working across tenants: provisioning workspaces, enabling modules, setting memberships. In here you are a guest — the entry point for the day is still this inbox.
platformAdmin.derStrukturbaumIstDein: The structure tree is your fastest health check after provisioning: are there value streams and ARTs, or is the customer still stuck setting up?
platformAdmin.jedeZustandsaenderndeAktionLandet: Every state-changing action lands here, role grants included. The filter bar gets you to the right event in seconds when questions come up.

tenantAdmin.mission: You set up the workspace and keep it workable: the right people with the right rights, the organisation mapped correctly.
tenantAdmin.nutzerEinladenRollenVergeben: Invite users, grant roles and set their visibility scopes.
tenantAdmin.getrenntDavonFestlegenWelche: Separately, define which role holds which permission.
tenantAdmin.dieOrganisationAbbildenWertstroeme: Map the organisation: create and maintain value streams and ARTs.
tenantAdmin.beiRueckfragenAusAudit: Answer questions from audit or compliance.
tenantAdmin.duUebernimmstVonDer: You take over from the platform: the workspace exists, you bring it to life.
tenantAdmin.duUebergibstAnPortfolio: You hand over to portfolio managers and RTEs: once structure and roles are in place, the real work starts.
tenantAdmin.derSetupGuideGibt: The setup guide sets the order
tenantAdmin.dieseListeIstDeine: This list is your daily starting point: who is there, which role they hold, whether anyone is suspended. A click opens the detail pane with the roles on the right.
tenantAdmin.werNutzerEinlaedtUnd: Who invites users and who grants rights are deliberately two separate powers. On the left you pick the role, on the right you see every action and where it deviates from the default.
tenantAdmin.wertstroemeFinanzierenEpicsOhne: Value streams fund epics — without them the portfolio stays empty. The button sits in the header of the structure page; you create ARTs afterwards on the detail page of the respective value stream.
tenantAdmin.dieKarteZeigtJe: The map shows one lane per value stream, the ARTs inside it as columns and their solutions as tiles. A click leads to the node's detail page — that is where you maintain the accountable people and create further ARTs.
tenantAdmin.ohneWiederkehrendenPiTakt: Without a recurring PI rhythm there is no planning. This milestone takes you to the timelines the ARTs subscribe to.
tenantAdmin.beiRueckfragenAusAudit2: When audit or compliance asks, you filter here by actor, action or period. Role grants are in there too.
tenantAdmin.achtMeilensteineVonWorkspace: Eight milestones from “workspace alive” to “first PI running”. You set the pace, the order is fixed — and you are the only one who may tick things off here.
tenantAdmin.ueberEinladenOeffnestDu: “Invite” opens the form on the right. After the assignment the invited person sees the same welcome dialog you have just seen — so your choice of role decides what gets explained to them.

portfolioManager.mission: You lead the portfolio: you decide what gets worked on, fund it, and in the end demonstrate what it delivered.
portfolioManager.denZielzustandUndDie: Set the target state and the top goals of the organisation.
portfolioManager.dieOrganisationAufbauenWertstroeme: Build the organisation: create value streams and the ARTs inside them.
portfolioManager.epicsDurchDenInvestment: Steer epics through the investment funnel and request or sign off maturity changes.
portfolioManager.denReifegradWechselAuf: Sign off the maturity change to L1 — that releases the benefit hypothesis.
portfolioManager.dasBudgetAufDie: Distribute the budget across the epics.
portfolioManager.denRealisiertenMehrwertIm: Track the realised value in the portfolio review.
portfolioManager.risikenFinalBewertenDu: Assess risks finally — you are the only one allowed to delete one.
portfolioManager.duUebernimmstVomEpic: You take over from the epic owner: they submit the hypothesis and business case, you decide.
portfolioManager.duUebergibstAnDen: You hand over to the RTE: once an epic is funded, they plan the implementation in the ART.
portfolioManager.derTagBeginntBei: The day begins with the goals
portfolioManager.hierStehenZielbildUnd: The target picture and the top goals live here. Every epic later contributes to one of them — without maintained goals no value can be demonstrated at year end.
portfolioManager.derPortfolioStandAuf: The portfolio state at a glance
portfolioManager.dasBoardStelltAlle: The board arranges all epics in a grid: columns are the maturity levels L0–L5, rows the investment horizons H3 to H0. What piles up on the left is undecided; what stands on the right is already running.
portfolioManager.inDerEpicListe: In the epic list you see where each epic stands in the investment funnel. A maturity change never happens by itself: it is requested on the epic and signed off by the people named for it.
portfolioManager.jeHalbjahrEineKachel: One tile per half-year, and the bar above names its state: current tile, pot, submissions, last state. The pot is the frame everything else is calculated against.
portfolioManager.verteiltWirdInDer: Distribution happens in the tile: the groups propose, the result sets the final amounts. An allocation greater than zero satisfies the blocking criterion for the step to L3.2 — the investment decision itself is the request plus the sign-off by VMO and finance.
portfolioManager.diePortfolioUebersichtIst: The portfolio overview is the surface for that meeting: funding pot and goals at the top, the kanban with the state of the initiatives below, the risks at the bottom. Whatever stalls here belongs on the agenda.
portfolioManager.dieMatrixStelltEintrittswahrscheinlichke: The matrix plots likelihood against impact — one mark per head issue, nested ones count in their head. Several marks in the top right corner are your signal to act before the next review.
portfolioManager.beantragteReifegradWechselUnd: Requested maturity changes and business cases wait in “My tasks”, stacked below your other work. Approve or reject with a reason — as long as you do nothing, the epic stands still.
portfolioManager.ueberDerListeFiltert: Above the list the ROAM bar filters by classification — open, resolved, owned, accepted, mitigated, each with a counter. “Open” is the set still to be decided. You are the only one who may also delete a risk.

valueStreamOwner.mission: You are accountable for a value stream: which initiatives arise there, whether they hold up, and who works them out.
valueStreamOwner.epicsInDeinemWertstrom: Create and sharpen epics in your value stream.
valueStreamOwner.einenEpicOwnerBenennen: Name an epic owner who takes on the elaboration.
valueStreamOwner.alsBenannterAbnehmerUeber: Decide on maturity changes as a named approver.
valueStreamOwner.dasWertstromBudgetAuf: Distribute the value stream budget across the ARTs.
valueStreamOwner.duUebernimmstVomPortfolio: You take over from the portfolio manager: your value stream receives a funding frame.
valueStreamOwner.duUebergibstAnDen: You hand over to the epic owner: they work out what you commissioned.
valueStreamOwner.imBaumFindestDu: In the tree you find your value stream with the ARTs hanging off it. Your write rights apply exactly here — outside you can read, but change nothing.
valueStreamOwner.neueEpicsDeinesWertstroms: New epics of your value stream are created here. You create them and then name an epic owner who works out the hypothesis and business case.
valueStreamOwner.derReifegradFunnelZeigt: The maturity funnel shows what is still being worked out and what is already running. The filter bar narrows it down to your value stream.
valueStreamOwner.derFinanzierungsrahmenDeinesWertstroms: Your value stream's funding frame is broken down onto the ARTs in controlling. Your value stream's detail page takes you there.
valueStreamOwner.vorschlagenDarfJederDein: Anyone may propose. Your proposal goes to the epic owner, who reviews and documents it — only then does it get a number.
valueStreamOwner.woDuAlsAbnehmer: Wherever you are named as an approver, the decision appears in “My tasks”. Only approval works without a reason — a rejection requires text.

epicOwner.mission: You work out epics: you formulate what the initiative should deliver, back it up and submit it for a decision.
epicOwner.dieBenefitHypotheseFormulieren: Formulate the benefit hypothesis and request the change to L1.
epicOwner.denBusinessCaseAusarbeiten: Work out the business case and request the change to L3.1 — its sign-off is the release.
epicOwner.risikenDeinesEpicsDokumentieren: Document, assess and ROAM-classify the risks of your epic.
epicOwner.nachEinerAblehnungUeberarbeiten: Revise after a rejection and request again.
epicOwner.duUebernimmstVomWertstrom: You take over from the value stream owner: they commission, you work it out.
epicOwner.duUebergibstAnPortfolio: You hand over to portfolio managers and approvers — deliberately, you may not decide on your own epic.
epicOwner.hierLiegenDieVorhaben: Here are the initiatives you are accountable for. A click on an epic opens the detail view — that is where your actual work happens.
epicOwner.titelUndWertstromGenuegen: Title and value stream are enough to start. Everything else — hypothesis, business case, deliverables — follows tab by tab.
epicOwner.dieReiterSindDeine: The tabs are your order of work
epicOwner.inEinemGeoeffnetenEpic: Inside an opened epic the tab bar guides you through the elaboration: overview, maturity timeline, hypothesis, business case, deliverables, dependencies, KPI & benefit. Work through them in order — on narrow screens the bar sits at the top instead of the left.
epicOwner.derDritteReiterDirekt: The third tab, right behind the maturity timeline. Once it is worked out you request the change to L1; with the sign-off the hypothesis is released — the starting shot for the business case.
epicOwner.kostenNutzenZeitraumSteht: Cost, benefit, timeframe. Once the content holds, you request the change to L3.1 — the sign-off by the five parties is the release of the business case.
epicOwner.beimAntragAufL: When requesting L3.1 you set who signs for which party. Your own approval is not provided for: whoever works it out does not decide.
epicOwner.vorschlagenDarfJederPruefen: Anyone may propose — reviewing and documenting is your job. Only with your acceptance does a risk get its number and become part of the register.
epicOwner.dieRisikenDeinesEpics: Assess the risks of your epic
epicOwner.wahrscheinlichkeitMalAuswirkungErgibt: Likelihood times impact gives the exposure. Every re-assessment is kept as a trace, so it becomes visible whether your measures work.

rte.mission: You orchestrate your agile release train: you keep the rhythm, plan the implementation and clear away what blocks delivery.
rte.programIncrementsAnlegenStarten: Create, start and close program increments.
rte.dasFeatureBacklogDes: Maintain the ART's feature backlog and set the delivery status.
rte.abhaengigkeitenZwischenVorhabenSichtbar: Make dependencies between initiatives visible and resolve them.
rte.risikenUndBlockadenDer: Document and ROAM-classify risks and blockers of the implementation.
rte.duUebernimmstVomPortfolio: You take over from the portfolio: funded epics become planned work with you.
rte.duUebergibstZurueckAns: You hand back to the portfolio: once the first feature goes into implementation, the epic is ready for the requested step to L4.
rte.derTagBeginntIn: The day begins in the inbox
rte.dasUmsetzungsCockpitIst: The delivery cockpit is your control room
rte.vierSichtenAufDieselben: Four views on the same features: board, table, roadmap, network. You switch depending on the question — board for flow, table for maintaining.
rte.woStehtDerZug: Where does the train stand in the PI?
rte.derStreifenZeigtDie: The strip shows the coming program increments, the current one highlighted. It is your sense of time for everything below it.
rte.hierSiehstDuJedes: Here you see every feature with title, ART, PI, status, WSJF and blockers in one row. This is the view in which you actually change things.
rte.inDerStatusSpalte: In the status column of each row you choose directly: approved, in progress, blocked, completed, cancelled. The first started feature satisfies the criterion with which the epic's change to L4 is requested.
rte.gerichteteVerknuepfungenZwischenVorhaben: Directed links between initiatives, cycle-checked. The type filter shows you the real blockers first — whatever stays open here gets expensive in planning.
rte.eineTimelineIstDer: A timeline is the shared PI rhythm several ARTs subscribe to. Without it there are no PIs — which is why it is the prerequisite for everything above.
rte.wasDieLieferungGefaehrdet: What endangers delivery belongs in the register, not in your head. You may document and set ROAM — accepting other people's proposals is the epic owner's job.
rte.woDuAlsStakeholder: Wherever you are named as a stakeholder, the decisions wait in “My tasks”. Skim them before you go into the cockpit — otherwise approvals block other people's planning.
rte.risikenUndBlockadenLiegen: Risks and blockers sit in one register. The bar filters by classification — open, resolved, owned, accepted, mitigated. Whatever stays on “open” holds up your PI closing in the end.

featureOwner.mission: You are accountable for the initiatives of your train: what gets built next, in which order and with what benefit.
featureOwner.nachWsjfPriorisierenDie: Prioritise by WSJF — the order is your statement.
featureOwner.denLieferstatusDeinerFeatures: Keep the delivery status of your features current.
featureOwner.abhaengigkeitenDeinerFeaturesBenennen: Name the dependencies of your features.
featureOwner.risikenUndBlockadenMelden: Report risks and blockers — the RTE classifies them.
featureOwner.duUebernimmstVomEpic: You take over from the epic owner: a funded epic is broken down into features with you.
featureOwner.duUebergibstAnDen: You hand over to the RTE: they schedule your prioritised features into a PI.
featureOwner.dasCockpitZeigtDie: The cockpit shows your train's features in four views. For daily maintenance the table is the right one.
featureOwner.deinBacklogInEiner: Your backlog, one row per feature
featureOwner.titelArtPiStatus: Title, ART, PI, status, WSJF and blockers side by side. A click on the title opens the detail view with description and dependencies.
featureOwner.dieWsjfSpalteMacht: The WSJF column makes the order justifiable rather than negotiable. The assessment happens in the feature's detail view; the number in the table is only the result.
featureOwner.wasVonAnderenAbhaengt: What depends on others belongs made visible — in the cockpit's network view or in the feature's detail. This overview shows the overall state.
featureOwner.einRisikoOderEine: Report a risk or a blocker
featureOwner.wasDuBeimBauen: What you see while building, nobody else knows. Risks and blockers take the same route: a proposal costs you two sentences, the epic owner reviews it. Classifying and closing is the RTE's job — deliberately separated so that report and resolution are not the same hand.
featureOwner.dieStatusSpalteIst: The status column is your promise to the rest of the train. A feature that has been “in progress” for weeks costs you credibility in planning.

viewer.mission: You follow how the portfolio is doing — with full read access to everything happening in your workspace.
viewer.portfolioFortschrittUndLieferstand: Follow portfolio progress and delivery state.
viewer.risikenVorschlagenDasIst: Propose risks — that is the one thing you may write, too.
viewer.duUebergibstAnDen: You hand over to the epic owner: a risk you proposed is reviewed and documented by them.
viewer.dasBoardStelltAlle: The board arranges all epics in a grid: columns are the maturity levels, rows the investment horizons. The undecided on the left, the running on the right — the fastest overview there is.
viewer.wahrscheinlichkeitGegenAuswirkungWas: Likelihood against impact. Whatever sits in the top right should come up in your next steering meeting.
viewer.dasEineWasAuch: The one thing you may write too
viewer.einRisikoVorschlagenDer: Propose a risk. The epic owner reviews it; only with their acceptance does it become a numbered entry in the register.

h3.blurb: Evaluating / R&D — no solution yet, only ideas, spikes and prototypes.

h2.blurb: Emerging — a new solution takes shape and is tested in the market as an MVP.
h2.epicArt: Emerging epics (building the MVP, market test)

h1.blurb: Investing & extracting — established core solution, carries the main revenue.

h0.blurb: Decommissioning — solution at end of life, shut down in an orderly way.
h0.budgetFokus: Reduce the run budget to 0 (OpEx wind-down)

concept.solutionVsEpic: A solution is the long-lived product or system (it generates ongoing operating cost, run). An epic is a large, time-bounded change to a solution (grow). The primary solution determines the epic's investment horizon — except in H3: there is no solution there, and the initiative carries its horizon itself.
concept.grow: Grow = Σ implementation cost of this solution's running epics (investment in further development).
concept.run: Run = Σ of the run-the-business items attributed to this solution, calculated over one year (maintenance, support, infrastructure). They are maintained in the budgeting module — each item with its own period; items spanning value streams count towards no solution.
